summary:
"Regolith Rescue: NASA Data Translator" is an interactive, pixel-art lunar exploration game designed to make NASA's scientific data more accessible and engaging. Players take the role of a junior lunar research scientist exploring a Moon-based research outpost, collecting scientific information and using interactive research terminals to interpret measurements, understand scientific units, examine visualizations and make informed decisions.

Inspired by NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), particularly the Diviner Lunar Radiometer instrument, the game introduces concepts such as lunar surface temperatures and regolith-related exploration challenges. It distinguishes real scientific observations from simplified gameplay simulations to maintain scientific accuracy.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with Google AI Studio assisting in code generation, development and prototyping. Visual Studio Code was used as the development environment, and Vercel was used for deployment.

Our goal is to transform complex lunar research into an interactive learning experience that encourages scientific curiosity, data literacy and interest in future space exploration.
details:
Project Details: Regolith Rescue

Regolith Rescue is an interactive educational game inspired by NASA's research on lunar regolith (the loose dust, soil, and rocky material covering the Moon's surface). The project aims to introduce players to the challenges of lunar exploration through an engaging, game-based experience rather than traditional quizzes or text-heavy educational materials.

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

Regolith Rescue transforms the scientific concept of lunar dust into an interactive gaming experience. Players engage with a lunar environment and encounter challenges inspired by the conditions and difficulties of exploring the Moon. Through gameplay, they can develop a better understanding of lunar regolith and why it matters for future lunar missions.

The project draws inspiration from NASA lunar datasets, particularly data associated with the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), to connect the gaming experience with actual lunar research.

2. What are its benefits?

  • Makes lunar science more accessible and enjoyable, especially for younger audiences.
  • Encourages learning through interaction and experimentation.
  • Introduces players to lunar regolith and its importance in space exploration.
  • Raises awareness of the challenges astronauts, equipment, and future lunar infrastructure may face.
  • Combines entertainment with informal STEM education.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to make space science less intimidating and more approachable. Many people are fascinated by the Moon but may not understand the environmental challenges involved in exploring it. Regolith Rescue attempts to bridge that gap by turning scientific concepts into an interactive experience.

We hope the project encourages curiosity about planetary science, NASA's lunar research, and the future of human exploration beyond Earth.

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software were used?

The project was developed using accessible web technologies:

  • HTML – Game structure and interface.
  • CSS – Visual design, layout, animations, and styling.
  • JavaScript – Game mechanics, interactions, and functionality.
  • Google AI Studio – AI-assisted development and prototyping.
  • NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) datasets – Scientific reference material and inspiration.
  • Visual Studio Code – Development environment.
  • Vercel – Hosting and deployment of the playable web game.

The project was designed as a browser-based game, eliminating the need for specialized hardware or software installations.

5. How is the project creative?

The creative aspect of Regolith Rescue lies in presenting lunar science as an interactive game instead of a conventional educational presentation or quiz.

Rather than simply explaining lunar regolith through paragraphs of information, the project uses gameplay to make the subject more engaging. It combines scientific inspiration, interactive design, and accessible web development to create an experience that can reach people who might not normally engage with space science.

We also focused on making the game visually approachable and easy to access through a web browser.

6. What factors did we consider during development?

Several factors influenced our development decisions:

  • Scientific relevance: Keeping the game connected to real lunar research and NASA datasets.
  • Educational value: Ensuring that gameplay communicates something meaningful about lunar exploration.
  • Accessibility: Making the game playable through an ordinary web browser without requiring expensive equipment.
  • User experience: Creating intuitive controls and an interactive experience that does not feel like a traditional quiz.
  • Technical limitations: Working within the time, resources, and development experience available to us.
  • Creativity: Finding a way to communicate a scientific subject through an enjoyable gaming format.

Ultimately, Regolith Rescue represents an attempt to bring lunar science closer to everyday audiences by combining research-inspired ideas with interactive entertainment.
